articles.title: When Stocks Dampen Festive Cheer, Can Bonds Keep the Celebrations Going?
articles.desc: Investors in India are navigating a challenging landscape as the equity markets descend into significant losses. Selling off assets at this juncture could incur financial damage, yet deferring such decisions may hinder urgent expenses. By maintaining fixed-income portfolios, investors can secure consistent cash flow to address short-term needs. To enhance portfolio resilience, diversifying between stocks and bonds becomes vital for achieving growth while safeguarding capital for future endeavors.

However, rising inflation, potential ECB rate hikes and political uncertainty in France continued to shape market sentiment and influence European debt markets.

articles.title: Centre issues advisory to states to boost fodder production, livestock infra under VB-G RAM G
articles.desc: The Centre has issued an advisory to states and Union territories to improve fodder security and livestock infrastructure. This advisory promotes convergence under the Viksit Bharat-Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission Act, 2025. It identifies 22 permissible works supporting fodder cultivation, livestock shelters, and veterinary health facilities. States are encouraged to increase expenditure on these works while aligning with local development priorities.

articles.title: Centre proposing parity in mineral taxation, states' rights to remain intact: Union Mines Secretary
articles.desc: Proposed amendments to the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act are intended to create tax parity across states. This initiative aims to reduce reliance on imports by fostering local production and processing of critical minerals. The Indian government has introduced significant subsidies to support industries establishing lithium and nickel processing facilities. Approximately 58 entities are now registered under a recycling program for electronic waste.

articles.title: EPL Q2 Results: Profit rises 4% YoY to Rs 111 crore
articles.desc: EPL reported a notable 4.52% increase in net profit, reaching Rs 110.9 crore for the September quarter of FY27. With revenues from operations climbing to Rs 1,567.4 crore, a 30% year-on-year growth, the Beauty & Cosmetics and Oral Care segments played pivotal roles. Despite higher expenses, the EBITDA margins held strong above 20%. Looking forward, EPL is set to focus on sustained revenue growth and stable profit margins.

articles.title: Blinkit Ambulance to charge Rs 2,500 for non-emergency trips; emergency service will stay free: Deepinder Goyal
articles.desc: Goyal said Blinkit Ambulance has served about 42,000 cases in the last two years, of which roughly 20,000 were emergencies. None were charged but a growing share of bookings were for routine checkups, hospital visits and hospital-to-home transfers, trips that “an Uber or private transport could have handled just as easily,” he said.

articles.title: China blocks SoftBank's $5.4 billion takeover of ABB's robotics division: FT
articles.desc: Softbank had agreed to buy ABB's robotics business in October last year, as CEO Masayoshi Son sought to establish SoftBank as a core player in the development of artificial intelligence.

articles.title: India bonds climb in step with Treasuries as oil sinks
articles.desc: Indian government bonds increased for the fourth consecutive session following a Democratic win in the US midterm elections. This victory led to a decline in crude oil prices, easing inflation concerns for India. The 10-year US Treasury yield also fell significantly, impacting investors' expectations. A trader noted that upcoming inflation data would be critical for assessing the Reserve Bank of India's rate outlook.

articles.title: South Korea plans to expand anti-piracy operations closer to Hormuz Strait
articles.desc: Seoul proposes extending its Cheonghae unit’s patrols to waters near Oman’s Duqm amid US pressure over Iran war.

articles.title: AI to reshape India's office space demand, workforce seen at 48 million by 2030: Report
articles.desc: AI is expected to change the nature of India's office space demand rather than reduce it, with the country's office-using workforce projected to grow from around 38 million in 2025 to 48 million by 2030, according to a study by Cushman & Wakefield.

articles.title: Sitaram Denims India files IPO papers with Sebi
articles.desc: Sitaram Denims India Ltd plans to launch an initial public offering with two components. The IPO includes a fresh issue of equity shares and an offer for sale by promoters. Proceeds from the fresh issue will be used for various purposes including repayment of borrowings and working capital requirements. The company aims to set up a new garment manufacturing facility in Bhilwara to expand capacity.

articles.desc: Alphabet shares rallied nearly 5% amid shifting US regulatory expectations, strong Google Cloud growth and investor focus on massive AI infrastructure spending, rising debt and long-term investment returns.

articles.title: Google unveils $15 billion data centre investment in Malaysia
articles.desc: Google announced plans on Wednesday to invest $15 billion in Malaysia over the next two years to build data centres and other infrastructure as demand booms for artificial intelligence services. It said the $15 billion investment will be made "over the next two years (2027 to 2028)", expanding on a $2 billion investment announced in 2024.

articles.title: US midterm outcome offers limited relief to India; oil, Russia sanctions remain key risks: Report
articles.desc: The outcome of the US midterm elections is expected to offer only marginal relief to India. Crude oil prices and potential tariffs on Russian oil purchases will continue to present economic challenges. While a Democratic majority may enhance diplomatic engagement, immediate trade relief seems unlikely. The rupee and foreign portfolio investor inflows could see some positive impact.

The feature was switched on by default for students at schools that had already enabled Gemini.

articles.title: Figma banking on AI credits, in-house model to lift margins
articles.desc: Figma is leaning on cashing in on its AI features through credits and using its first-party model to power tasks on its design software platform to bolster its margins, finance chief Praveer Melwani told Reuters on Wednesday.

articles.desc: S Jaishankar recently met with Guyana President Irfaan Ali to review their bilateral cooperation agreements. They discussed the implementation of a UPI-like system and the extension of a USD 500 million Line of Credit. Additionally, agreements were signed for manufacturing projects and Quick Impact Projects in Guyana. Jaishankar also engaged with leaders from Australia and the United Kingdom to strengthen economic partnerships.

articles.title: OpenAI, ready to IPO in 2027, now counts majority of sales from enterprises, Greg Brockman says
articles.desc: OpenAI President Greg Brockman said on Wednesday the company now generates the majority of its revenue from enterprise sales and he believes it will be ready to go public in 2027.

articles.title: OpenAI to acquire developer tools firm Pierre to expand Codex capabilities
articles.desc: OpenAI will acquire Pierre Computer Company, the developer of open-source coding tools, to expand its Codex platform's capabilities in building, understanding and reviewing software, as it looks to strengthen the role of AI agents across the software development process.

articles.title: Apple cuts employee AI budgets in cost-control push
articles.desc: Apple has reduced employee budgets for AI usage as part of a broader effort to rein in costs, even as it seeks to expand the use of AI across its operations, Bloomberg News reported on Wednesday, citing people familiar with the matter.

articles.title: Goldman, Apollo seek buyers for $40 billion SpaceX AI chip deal
articles.desc: Goldman Sachs and Apollo Global Management are in talks with investors to sell portions of a roughly $40 billion financing deal for SpaceX's AI chips, Bloomberg News reported on Wednesday.

articles.title: EAM Jaishankar discusses economic partnership, CETA with UK’s Burnham on CHOGM sidelines
articles.desc: S Jaishankar met UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham in Antigua and Barbuda for CHOGM 2026 discussions. They focused on strengthening economic partnerships under the Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement. Jaishankar emphasized the importance of digital solutions and climate initiatives during a Commonwealth meeting. He highlighted local distribution networks and the role of the Indian business community in fostering connections.

articles.title: US sanctions India-based couple, companies over alleged support for Iran's Shadow oil fleet
articles.desc: The United States imposed sanctions on Suniel Kumar Sharma and Jaspreet Preeti Shahid for aiding Iran's shadow fleet. Their network allegedly provided fraudulent maritime registrations to help sanctioned vessels transport Iranian petroleum. Several companies linked to the couple also received sanctions under Executive Order 13902. Additionally, a Turkiye-based company was sanctioned for providing services to US-designated Iranian airlines.

articles.title: Interest rates expected to rise for first time in over three years
articles.desc: Most analysts are predicting an increase from 3.75% to 4%, the first increase in more than three years.

articles.title: Qualcomm is betting big on data centers as smartphone sales sink
articles.desc: With smartphone sales tanking by around 20 percent compared to 2025, Qualcomm is looking to data centers to help boost its bottom line. During its Q4 2026 earnings call, the company laid out its plans to make a splash in the AI data center business, through partnerships with companies like Amazon and Meta announced earlier […]

articles.title: Anthony Zurcher: Trump is weakened but still wields power for now
articles.desc: Trump has given conflicting messages about how he might deal with Democrats in Congress after his party's resounding defeat.

articles.title: Big factories dominate India's manufacturing output, Annual Survey of Industries shows
articles.desc: India's manufacturing sector is characterised by a significant concentration in large factories generating substantial output. Factories producing over ₹500 crore contribute to more than three-fifths of total value added. Smaller factories represent a large number but have minimal output and value contribution.

articles.title: New orders & robust demand lift India's October services growth to 4-month high
articles.desc: Growth in India's services sector increased to a four-month high in October due to strong domestic demand and business orders. The HSBC Services Business Activity Index rose to 55.8, reflecting improved business conditions. Conversely, manufacturing activity showed a slight decline, easing to a PMI of 54.7. While input prices continued to rise, the rate of increase was the slowest in over six years.

articles.title: US slaps sanctions on Indian, Turkish firms and people for aiding Iran
articles.desc: The sanctions are part of the Trump administration's "Operation Economic Outcast," which aims to cut off Iran's ability to sell oil to fund the war with the US and Israel. Treasury unveiled the new sanctions a day after Democrats made huge gains in midterm elections, winning control of both houses of Congress as voters expressed anger about the Iran war and its impact in fueling US inflation.

articles.title: Over half of street vendors may cut UPI acceptance if 0.4% MDR is introduced: ISB study
articles.desc: More than 67% of street vendors in India currently accept UPI payments for transactions. A proposed 0.4% merchant discount rate could lead to reduced acceptance among vendors. Concerns arise particularly for vendor-supplier transactions, as many vendors make payments above ₹2,000. A significant portion of vendors faced additional charges from suppliers and might pass costs onto customers.

articles.title: Government prepares draft sustainable aviation fuels policy; moots mandatory blending in ATF from 2027
articles.desc: The civil aviation ministry has circulated the draft National Policy on Sustainable Aviation Fuels which mandates use of only indigenously manufactured SAF to be blended with Aviation Turbine Fuel (ATF).

articles.title: Piyush Goyal sets March 2027 deadline for digitisation of DGFT services, aims to end physical visits
articles.desc: Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal has set March 31, 2027, as the deadline for complete digitisation of DGFT services, including licence, permit and SCOMET approvals. From April 1, businesses will no longer need physical visits to government offices for these services. The move also includes digitising historical records and simplifying procedures.

articles.title: Lenskart, Nykaa, PhysicsWallah see Q2 profits surge
articles.desc: New-age companies Nykaa, Lenskart, and PhysicsWallah reported strong numbers for the September quarter. This and more in today’s ETtech Top 5.

articles.title: Uber's profit forecast disappoints as driver shortages, Middle East conflict hurt
articles.desc: The company is responding by spending more to recruit and retain drivers, a cost that will be watched closely because it comes as the company also funds a major push into autonomous vehicles and a string of acquisitions.
